## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 42 (*Sabbahattha*, "Putting whole hand in mouth") is a training rule (*sekhiya*) belonging to the Suttavibhaṅga of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Formulated as part of the monastic code governing table etiquette and decorum, the rule concerns not putting the whole hand into the mouth while eating [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the rule has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali, one of three translations in three languages documented by SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

The rule possesses extensive parallels across various early Buddhist vinaya traditions. In Pali literature, it directly corresponds to the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha rule (*pli-tv-bu-pm-sk42*), the Bhikkhu Parivāra (*Sekhiya 42*), and the parallel disciplinary codes for nuns: Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 42, Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha Sekhiya 42, and the Bhikkhunī Parivāra [SuttaCentral]. Chinese parallels include the Sarvāstivāda Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (*Lzh Sarv Bu Vb Sk65*) and Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga/Prātimokṣa texts, the Dharmaguptaka Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅgas and Prātimokṣas (e.g., *Lzh Dg Bu Vb Sk 46*), and the Upāliparipṛcchā (*lzh-upp-bu-sk37*) [SuttaCentral].
